solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Form bad character, the way some artists work

indicators.note: bad here means spoilt or out of shape, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: your nature is your character or disposition

explanation.surface: An instruction to shape a bad character, followed by a remark about how some painters go about things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like a verb or a shape, but it is only fodder; 'character' is a person's nature, not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting from nature means working directly from real scenes or models rather than from memory or imagination.

clue.text: Star laughing about for example receiving diamonds

indicators.note: about means going around, so the outer word wraps the rest

parts.note: riant is a literary word for laughing or cheerful, from French

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so EG holds the diamonds letter

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A celebrity, laughing, is handed some diamonds as an example of their reward.
explanation.walkthrough: Riant is a rare literary word for laughing, borrowed from French.
explanation.definitionFit: A red giant is a large, cool, late-stage star, such as Betelgeuse, in astronomy.

clue.text: Staff's shaggy hair cut

indicators.note: cut means docked at the end, so the final letter of the hair word is lost

parts.note: a mane is a long shaggy head of hair, as on a horse or lion

explanation.surface: An office worker's untidy hair has been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff's' reads as 'Staff is'; the 's is a link. MANE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To man a desk or ship is to staff it, providing the people who work it.

clue.text: Down with heroin? Shame!

parts.note: French a bas means down with, a cry against something
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A campaigner's cry against heroin, ending in disgust at the drug.
explanation.walkthrough: A BAS is French for 'down with', a protester's slogan used in English too.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash someone is to make them feel embarrassed or ashamed, so it is a verb meaning to put to shame.

clue.text: Hesitate, being lawyer, to put husband last

indicators.note: to put signals that one letter is taken from its place and set elsewhere
last says where it goes: at the very end of the string

parts.note: a human being, here just a being
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy tables

explanation.surface: Someone dithers about joining the legal profession and leaves marriage till later.
explanation.walkthrough: HUMAN plus DA gives HUMANDA; moving the H for husband to the end gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To um and ah is the British idiom for dithering or making hesitant noises before deciding.

clue.text: Under the influence, neighbours at table were singing

parts.note: at the bridge table East and North sit next to each other, E and N
chanted means were singing, in a rhythmic way

explanation.surface: Drunk dinner guests at the next seats began singing.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge the four players are named North, East, South and West; E and N are adjacent seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone enchanted is under a spell, under the influence of a magic charm.

clue.text: A little gem is only paste

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tiny jewel is merely an imitation made of paste.
explanation.definitionFit: Miso is a Japanese fermented soybean paste used in soups and sauces, so it is an example.

clue.text: Make footballers out of form fear cut

parts.note: Man U is Manchester United, the English football club

indicators.note: out of form means not in their proper shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A team of footballers playing badly makes even their fear lessen.
explanation.walkthrough: FEAR CUT rearranged gives FACTURE after MAN U.
explanation.definitionFit: To manufacture something is to make or produce it, especially in a factory; a synonym.

clue.text: An hour in sleep, that's short for most retiring

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other
short means cut off before the end, so the final letter of the nap goes

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon sleep
H is the abbreviation for an hour

explanation.surface: Spending an hour asleep counts as a quick nap for the most bashful person.
explanation.walkthrough: SIESTA cut short is SIEST; H goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiest is the superlative of shy, so it describes the most bashful or reserved person, a synonym of retiring.

clue.text: Group of animals bidding farewell to paradise?

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden of paradise
ta-ta is an informal British way of saying goodbye

explanation.surface: Creatures saying goodbye as they leave paradise, like Adam and Eve's animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentata is an old taxonomic order of mammals lacking front teeth, such as sloths, anteaters and armadillos.

clue.text: Like some fruit, orange finally having fallen open

indicators.note: having fallen means dropped out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: candied fruit is preserved by boiling in sugar

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A fruit, like an orange, drops off and splits open.
explanation.walkthrough: CANDIED loses E, the final letter of 'orange'.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank and open, honest in speaking without hiding anything; a synonym.

clue.text: Fairly broad pepper pot, for one

explanation.walkthrough: Pepper pot here is not a cruet but a spicy Caribbean stew, so it is a WI (West Indian) DISH.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means somewhat, so widish is rather wide; split as WI DISH it names a West Indian meal.

clue.text: Fancy their sister, one with long hair

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is attracted to their sibling, who has lovely long hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish setter is a gundog breed known for its long silky red coat, so it is an example.

clue.text: Died fighting shark for example of unusual size

parts.note: war means fighting, as in at war
a shark is an example of a fish

explanation.surface: A creature of unusual size died fighting a shark.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwarfish means very small, like a dwarf, which is one kind of unusual stature.

clue.text: Hostile soldier maybe touching one arrested

indicators.note: arrested means held or detained, so these two words grip the one letter between them

parts.note: a soldier is one caste of ant
pathetic in its older sense means moving or touching
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hostile soldier, perhaps moved, has someone under arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldier ants are the defender caste of a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipathetic means feeling strong aversion or opposition, so hostile is a synonym.

clue.text: In a small pond, picked up litres in wooden butt

indicators.note: In puts all of this inside the pond phrase

parts.note: a pool is a small pond

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means lifted, so this piece is read upwards
in says the litres letter goes inside the wood

parts.note: fir describes something made of fir wood

explanation.surface: Litres of water collected in a small pond within a wooden barrel, or butt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butt' suggests a water barrel, matching the pond and wood, but it means the target of a joke; 'picked up' reads upwards in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An April fool is the victim of a prank on 1 April, the butt of the joke.

clue.text: Pleased room of horrors is filled with large blooms

parts.note: glad means pleased

indicators.note: is filled with means having something placed inside

parts.note: Room 101 is the torture room in Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four, written IOI

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased that a scary room has been filled with large flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 101 is read as the letters IOI.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli are tall plants with spikes of showy flowers, so they are examples of blooms.

clue.text: Horse roundly beaten in fearful fashion

indicators.note: beaten means battered out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A horse is thrashed soundly in a frightening way.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrendously means in a dreadful or horrifying manner, so fearful fashion is a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Take meal at a sort of bar and be humiliated

parts.note: to eat is to take a meal
a crowbar is a sort of bar, shortened to crow

explanation.surface: Someone has dinner at a certain kind of pub and is embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but CROW is short for the iron crowbar.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat crow is an American idiom for admitting one was wrong, being humbled.

clue.text: Twice make knight's move? Not me

definitions.note: the knight speaks: another chess piece, not the speaker

parts.note: bis means twice or again, as on a musical score
a knight in chess hops over other pieces

explanation.surface: A chess player asked to move a knight twice declines.
explanation.walkthrough: The knight is the one speaking, so 'Not me' points to a different chess piece, one that never hops.
explanation.definitionFit: The bishop is the chess piece that moves diagonally, a different piece from the knight saying 'me'.

clue.text: Appointment offers fortune, on paper

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper, the paper in question
your lot is your fortune or destiny

explanation.surface: A meeting with a fortune-teller is written down.
explanation.definitionFit: A time slot is a reserved period in a schedule, such as an appointment booked in a diary.

clue.text: Race round, part of a dash

parts.note: to race is to speed
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Running a lap is part of a sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash' looks like a sprint, but it is a car's dashboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedo, short for speedometer, is a dial on a car's dashboard.

clue.text: Pressure in narrow opening causes rupture

indicators.note: in says the pressure letter goes inside the opening

parts.note: a slit is a narrow opening
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: Pressure in a narrow gap makes something burst.
explanation.definitionFit: A split is a tear or break, so a rupture is a synonym.

clue.text: Greeting from the person that put round collector's item?

indicators.note: put round says the person word wraps around the item

parts.note: who means the person that
a hat is passed round to collect money

explanation.surface: A greeting from the one who passes round a valuable piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collector's item' suggests a valuable antique, but a hat is used to collect donations.
explanation.definitionFit: What ho is a jaunty, old-fashioned British hello, as used by Bertie Wooster.

clue.text: Narrative about love in classical speech

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: in says the love letter goes inside the language

parts.note: Latin is the language of classical Rome
O is love, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A story about love, told in the style of ancient orators.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a telling or account of events, so a narrative is a synonym.

clue.text: Front half of bicycle is a shade of brown

indicators.note: front half of keeps only the leading three of the six letters of the bike word

parts.note: a tandem is a bicycle for two

explanation.surface: The front of a bike is painted brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Tan is a light yellowish-brown colour, like tanned leather.

clue.text: Standard placed at south pole

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

explanation.surface: A flag is set up at the South Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pole' looks as if it goes with 'south', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole, such as a mast or boom on a ship.

clue.text: Wants linen laundered, several sets here maybe

indicators.note: laundered means washed and tumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wants their linen washed, perhaps several sets of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets' looks like sets of sheets, but a match in this game is played over several sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn tennis matches are scored in sets, so a game with several sets is played here.
